कुकर्दम

KUKARDAMA . A wicked monarch of Piṇḍārakadeśa. He had to be born in Pretayoni (womb of a ghostess) due to his many sins, and once he came to the āśrama of kahoḍa, and the sage recognised him as his former disciple and absolved him from his ghosthood. (padma purāṇa, uttara Khaṇḍa, Chapter 139).

कुक्कुर १

KUKKURA I . A King of the Lunar dynasty, the founder of the kukkura dynasty.

कुकुर १

KUKURA I . (KUKŪRA). A King of the vṛṣṇi dynasty. From vṛṣṇi the descendants are in the following order:--yudhājit--śini--satyaka--sātyaki (yuyudhāna)--jaya--Kuṇi--anamitra--pṛśni-citraratha--kukura. As kukura was a very reputed King his successors were also called Kukuras. The Kṣatriyas of this dynasty were subject to the orders of śrī kṛṣṇa. (Udyoga Parva, Chapter 28). Members of the kukura and andhaka dynasties became drunkards, and at last quarrelled with one another and died. (Mausala Parva, Chapter 3).

कुक्कुर २

KUKKURA II . A noble sage who distinguished himself in Dharmaputra's court. (Sabhā Parva, Chapter 4, Verse 19).

कुकुर २

KUKURA II . A serpent born in the kaśyapa dynasty. (Udyoga Parva, Chapter 103, Verse 10).

कुक्कुर म्

KUKKURA (M) . An urban region in ancient india. (bhīṣma parva, Chapter 9, Verse 42).

कुक्कुटिका

KUKKUṬIKĀ . A female attendant of skanda. (bhīṣma Parva, Chapter 46, Verse 15).

कुकुद्मिन्

KUKUDMIN . A son, Ānarta, was born to King śaryāti, the son of vaivasvata manu. revata, the famous Rājarṣi, who ruled from his capital at kuśasthalī island, was the son of Ānarta. Ānarta had hundred sons, the eldest being kukudmin, and also a daughter called revatī. (devī bhāgavata, 7th skandha).

कुकुरम्

KUKURA(M) . An urban region in ancient india. (bhīṣma parva, Chapter 9, Verse 60).

कुक्षि १

KUKṢI I . To svāyambhuva manu the son of brahmā were born two sons called priyavrata and uttānapāda by his wife śatarūpā, and kardama prajāpati married the daughter of priyavrata. And, to them were born three sons called samrāṭ, kukṣi and virāṭ. (agni purāṇa, Chapter 18).

कुक्षि २

KUKṢI II . A well known asura King. An aspect of this asura was later reborn as King pārvatīya. (Ādi Parva, Chapter 67, Verse 56).
